You are an experienced NSW HSC English marker. Mark the student's response to a question from the 2022 NSW HSC English Advanced exam, Paper 1 strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences. Judge expression only where the criteria reward it, and never comment on handwriting.

Question 4 [3 marks]: Analyse how Saramago conveys the value of memory in this extract.
STIMULUS / TEXTS PROVIDED:
Text 4 — Memoir extract
The house where I was born no longer exists, not that it matters, because I have no memory of having lived in it. The other house, the impoverished dwelling of my maternal grandparents, Josefa and Jerónimo, has also disappeared beneath a mound of rubble, the house which, for ten or twelve years, was my true home, in the most intimate and profound sense of the word, the magical cocoon in which the metamorphoses* vital to both the child and the adolescent took place. That loss, however, has long since ceased to cause me any suffering because, thanks to the memory’s reconstructive powers, I can, at any moment, rebuild its white walls, replant the olive tree that shaded the entrance, open and close the low front door and the gate to the vegetable garden where I once saw a small snake coiled and waiting, or I can go into the pigsties and watch the piglets suckling, enter the kitchen and pour from the jug into the chipped mug the water which, for the thousandth time, will quench that summer’s thirst. Then I say to my grandmother: ‘Grandma, I’m going for a walk.’ And she says: ‘Off you go, then’, but she doesn’t warn me to be careful, no, in those days, grown-ups had more confidence in the children they brought up.
JOSÉ SARAMAGO
Small Memories
Courtesy of the José Saramago Foundation
* metamorphoses   transformations

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 3):
3 marks: Analyses effectively how Saramago conveys the value of memory, using detailed, well-chosen evidence from the extract
2 marks: Analyses how Saramago conveys the value of memory, using well- chosen evidence from the extract
1 marks: Provides some relevant information about the value of memory

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
Saramago conveys memory as valuable because of its ‘reconstructive powers’ which allow people to revisit the past. He switches between past, present and future tense to highlight how memory helps us to relive past experiences. Through memory Saramago claims he can, ‘at any moment’, ‘rebuild’ his childhood house, ‘replant the olive tree’ and ‘go into the pigsties and watch the piglets’. These cumulative descriptions emphasise the value of memory, enabling him to return to his ‘true home’ even though it no longer exists. NESA   2022 HSC    English Advanced — Paper 1   Marking Guidelines
